messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int lives = 3;
if (lives = 1) printf("last life");

Question: What is lives afterwards?
The student answered: 3

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: `=` compares

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: Hinglish: romanised Hindi mixed with English programming words, 6 to 16 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["lives = 1 mein equals se compare hota hai, dono equal nahi, so lives 3 hi rahega", "if condition check karta hai ki lives 1 ke barabar hai ya nahi, equal nahi hai to change nahi hoga", "maine socha = comparison karta hai, 3 aur 1 match nahi karte, isliye lives 3 rehta hai", "printf tabhi chalega jab lives 1 ho, par lives 3 hai, so kuch change nahi hota", "lives ki value 3 hai aur = se check karne par 1 se equal nahi mila, so 3 hi raha"]}

sentences: lives = 1 mein equals se compare hota hai, dono equal nahi, so lives 3 hi rahega
if condition check karta hai ki lives 1 ke barabar hai ya nahi, equal nahi hai to change nahi hoga
maine socha = comparison karta hai, 3 aur 1 match nahi karte, isliye lives 3 rehta hai
printf tabhi chalega jab lives 1 ho, par lives 3 hai, so kuch change nahi hota
lives ki value 3 hai aur = se check karne par 1 se equal nahi mila, so 3 hi raha
